reports.title: Primary-Source Verification Update — August 2026
reports.summary: An August 2026 verification pass expands the tracker to 52 documented records, refreshes four FY2025 net-asset figures, resolves payment-percentage and trust-identity errors, and publishes 93 applicable primary-source PDFs across 24 trust detail pages.
highlights: 52 documented records: 51 active trusts and 1 closed trust
Four FY2025 annual reports refresh ASARCO, Combustion Engineering, Kaiser Gypsum, and Congoleum asset figures
93 applicable verified source PDFs now available directly on 24 trust detail pages
Separate sub-account documentation preserved for Owens Corning/Fibreboard and Federal-Mogul
Paddock plan-funding commitment removed from net assets; Kaiser Gypsum distinguished from Kaiser Aluminum

reports.title: State of the Asbestos Trust System — Q3 2026
reports.summary: The filing season closes with the documented floor confirmed at $17.04B and 23.3% on verified class-(a) footing. Maremont and API are now fully verified at FY2025, correcting a prior $933,980 under-verification. Seven cuts since January 2023, zero raises. Babcock & Wilcox completes the seven-week notice-to-cut template. No new formations or closures.
highlights: Documented floor confirmed at exact $17,042,880,106 — Maremont ($49.59M) and API ($7.73M) now fully verified at FY2025, correcting prior $933,980 under-verification
Seven documented cuts since January 2023, zero raises; B&W completes seven-week notice-to-cut template (4.7%→4.3%, June 30)
Three pending reconsiderations: Maremont (Apr 7, decision expected), USG (May, cut possible 12–24 months), B&W (ratification pending TAC/FCR consent)
No new formations or closures in Q3; Rapid-American remains most recent closure at 14 months (June 6, 2025)
DCPF governance consolidation continues: Cross-Trust Audit Program and TDP §5.5 amendments in effect across 10 trusts (~$8.7B, ~51% of documented floor)
Filing season closes with 23.3% of floor on verified class-(a) footing — highest documented share in the series
Six FY2025 reports still PACER-only (WRG, MLC, Armstrong, Flintkote, PCC, Celotex); largest remaining floor-quality upgrade available
Georgia-Pacific, DBMP/CertainTeed, and Trane remain in formation pipeline; no funded trusts this quarter

reports.title: State of the Asbestos Trust System — Q2 2026
reports.summary: Filing-season issue: nine trusts move onto FY2025 filed footing, refreshing the documented floor to an exact $17,042,880,106 (23.3% class-(a)); cuts at Combustion Engineering and Babcock & Wilcox, reconsideration notices at Maremont, USG, and B&W; Georgia-Pacific abandons Bestwall and plans a new Chapter 11. Retrospective issue, backfilled July 28, 2026.
highlights: Documented floor refreshed to an exact $17,042,880,106 — nine trusts (23.3%) now rest on filed FY2025/Q1 2026 documents
Two cuts: Combustion Engineering to 15.3% (April) and Babcock & Wilcox 4.7%→4.3% (June 30, 'until further notice')
Three reconsideration notices: Maremont (Apr 7), USG (May), B&W (May 7) — B&W's seven-week notice-to-cut is the documented template
Owens Corning Subfund cut in June; magnitude not yet documented — flagged, not estimated
Georgia-Pacific abandons Bestwall after eight years, plans a new Chapter 11; ~$1B+ trust expected but uncounted until funded
FY2025 season splits free vs. PACER-only: WRG, MLC, Armstrong, Flintkote, PCC, and Celotex exhibits sit behind PACER
DII's $121.1M 2025 claims expense and Manville's $5.33B cumulative payouts newly documented from filed reports

reports.title: State of the Asbestos Trust System — Q1 2026
reports.summary: NARCO resumes under DCPF administration, the Fourth Circuit's Herlihy decision channels ~60,000 stayed DBMP suits toward a future trust, the Bestwall fight reaches the Supreme Court docket, and the Cross-Trust Audit Program runs its first cycles — a quiet quarter for payment percentages. Retrospective issue, backfilled July 28, 2026.
highlights: No documented cuts or raises — a pause in the post-2023 cadence; trailing record: six cuts, zero raises in the tracked set
NARCO resumes intake January 12 under DCPF, completing the migration paused December 31; DCPF now administers ~51% of the documented floor
Herlihy v. DBMP (Feb 11): Fourth Circuit affirms denial of stay relief; ~60,000 stayed suits channel toward an eventual §524(g) trust
Bestwall fight moves to the Supreme Court docket — cert petition No. 25-1013 filed in February
Cross-Trust Audit Program runs its first monthly cycles; TDP §5.5 completes its first full quarter in effect
Floor composition unchanged at ≈$17.0B — the April filing season is the next data event

reports.title: State of the Asbestos Trust System — 2025 Year in Review
reports.summary: The 2025 year in review: four payment-percentage cuts and the Celotex deferral, Rapid-American's end-of-life, landmark Fourth Circuit rulings in Kaiser Gypsum and Bestwall, and DCPF's §5.5 amendments and Cross-Trust Audit Program consolidating governance across half the documented floor. Retrospective issue, backfilled July 28, 2026.
highlights: Documented floor ≈$17.0B; composition static all year — 32 secondary-carried trusts at exactly $13,076,231,337, nine public filers at FY2024 values
Four documented cuts in 2025: Kaiser (Feb), W.R. Grace (Apr), Quigley (Oct), Motors Liquidation (Dec); Celotex enters a Deferral Period at 7%
Zero raises in the tracked set; Shook & Fletcher's 50→58% raise (May) documents movement outside it
Rapid-American closes June 6, depleted — final payouts ~18–21%, the system's newest end-of-life data point
Fourth Circuit landmarks: Kaiser Gypsum confirmation affirmed (Apr 29); Bestwall jurisdiction upheld (Aug 1), en banc denied 8–6 (Oct 30)
Governance consolidation: TDP §5.5 amendments (Nov 14) and the Cross-Trust Audit Program (Dec 10–11) propagate across DCPF's ~$8.7B, ~51% of the floor
NARCO pauses intake December 31 ahead of DCPF administration — the year ends mid-transition
